questions.q: Why does this lesson split a single workflow into two separate jobs instead of one job that runs on both a PR and a push to main?
options: A PR and a real merge need different behavior — checking against a disposable CI schema versus deploying to real production
GitHub Actions technically cannot support two triggers in one workflow file
Two jobs run faster than one job, regardless of what they do
It's purely a stylistic preference with no functional reason
questions.explain: Conflating the two moments would either run untested PR code against production, or never actually deploy — two jobs with different conditions solve both problems.

questions.q: What does `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` do on a job?
options: Restricts that job to only run when the workflow was triggered by a pull request
Deletes the pull request automatically
Runs the job on every single trigger regardless of type
Has no effect unless combined with a schedule trigger
questions.explain: A job-level if: condition controls whether that specific job runs at all, based on what triggered the workflow.

questions.q: What does the `--target prod` flag do for dbt?
options: Switches which block of profiles.yml dbt reads, without changing the file's structure
Deletes all other targets from profiles.yml permanently
Only works when running dbt outside of CI
Renames the entire dbt project
questions.explain: --target selects which named output block (like ci or prod) dbt uses for its connection and schema, using the same profiles.yml structure.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does 'deploying' actually mean for a dbt project?
options: Running dbt build successfully against the real production schema — there's no server process to restart
Restarting a web server process, exactly like a typical application deploy
Manually copying files via FTP to a production server
dbt projects cannot be deployed at all
questions.explain: Unlike a web app, a dbt project has no running server — running dbt build against production, successfully, is the entire deployment.

questions.q: What does `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` check for in the deploy job's condition?
options: That the push landed directly on the main branch, not some other branch
That the repository has at least one open issue
That the workflow file itself hasn't changed
That a specific GitHub user triggered the push
questions.explain: github.ref reports the full ref of the branch being built; checking it equals refs/heads/main confirms this is a push directly to main.
